formation.title: The Banner of the Griffin
formation.text:
The red griffin spreads its wings across Pomerania. For five centuries the House of Griffin has ruled these Baltic shores, navigating between the ambitions of Brandenburg to the south and the autonomy of the great Hanseatic cities within their own borders. Now, with Pomerania united, a choice must be made about the duchy's future.

The Griffin dukes have long struggled to impose their authority over cities like Stralsund and Stettin, whose Hanseatic privileges grant them near-independence. Shall the duke assert his ancient rights and forge a centralized state? Or shall he embrace the commercial republic within his realm, ruling in partnership with the merchant oligarchs whose wealth built these shores?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Griffin's word is law in Pomerania

modifiers.name: The Griffin's Dominion
modifiers.text: Under the iron will of the Griffin dukes, Pomerania's fractious towns and restless barons have been brought to heel. The duchy speaks with one voice, the duke's.

options.text: Let the Hanseatic cities be our strength

modifiers.name: The Wendish Quarter
modifiers.text: Pomerania has embraced the Hanseatic spirit. Its cities govern themselves, its merchants sail freely, and its wealth flows from the counting houses of Stralsund and Stettin, not the ducal court.

advances.name: Wendish Shores
advances.text: The Slavic Pomeranians have fished these Baltic waters and harvested amber from its shores since time immemorial.

advances.name: Griffin Dukedom
advances.text: The House of Griffin, bearing its red heraldic beast since the 12th century, has established ducal authority over the Pomeranian lands.

advances.name: Christianization of Pomerania
advances.text: The conversion of the Pomeranian Slavs brought the duchy into the Latin Christian world, founding bishoprics and monasteries along the coast.

advances.name: Town Charters
advances.text: Pomeranian dukes granted municipal rights to coastal settlements, sparking the growth of towns that would become Hanseatic powerhouses.

advances.name: Hanseatic Membership
advances.text: Pomeranian towns have joined the Wendish quarter of the Hanseatic League, binding their fortunes to the greatest commercial network in northern Europe.

advances.name: Stralsund Emporium
advances.text: Stralsund has risen to become the second city of the Hanse, with 300 ships flying its banner across the Baltic.

advances.name: Herring Fairs
advances.text: The great herring fairs of the Baltic coast have made Pomeranian ports the center of the northern fish trade. On the herring coasts the towns keep their Vitten, where the catch is salted and packed.

advances.name: Greifswald University
advances.text: Founded in 1456 by Duke Wartislaw IX, the University of Greifswald is one of the oldest in northern Europe, drawing scholars from across the Hanseatic world.

event.title: The University at Greifswald
event.text:
On October 17, 1456, Duke Wartislaw IX of Pomerania-Wolgast inaugurated a new university at Greifswald, established through the initiative and generous patronage of the city's mayor, Heinrich Rubenow. With papal approval already secured, the institution opens its doors as one of the few centers of learning in the entire Baltic region.

The university draws students from across the Hanseatic world, Scandinavians, Livonians, and Germans gather to study law, theology, and the arts. Within its first decades, hundreds of foreign scholars will pass through its halls, making Greifswald a beacon of learning amid the commerce of the Wendish Hanse.

options.text: May knowledge flourish on these Baltic shores

advances.name: Baltic Fleet
advances.text: Pomeranian shipbuilders have expanded the duchy's fleet, establishing the coast as a center of maritime power.

advances.name: Stettin Emporium
advances.text: Stettin dominates Oder River commerce, with grain from the hinterland and salt from the coast passing through its bustling wharves.

event.title: The Emporium of the Oder
event.text: Stettin has secured its position as the gateway of the Oder. Grain from Brandenburg and Greater Poland flows downriver to Pomeranian ports, while salt and herring travel inland on the return. The city's forty guilds and bustling docks testify to its wealth. But this prosperity brings its own tension, shall the duchy's commercial future be guided by the league's collective discipline, or by the duke's direct hand?

modifiers.name: Hanseatic Zenith
modifiers.text: Pomerania's merchants stand at the summit of Baltic trade, their ships and counting houses the envy of the northern seas.

modifiers.name: Ducal Assertion
modifiers.text: The Griffin duke has reasserted control over the Hanseatic towns, bringing their revenues under ducal oversight.

advances.name: Baltic Amber Craft
advances.text: Pomeranian craftsmen have elevated amber-working into a fine art, creating jewelry and devotional objects prized across Europe.

advances.name: Burgher Autonomy
advances.text: The Hanseatic towns have secured legal privileges that limit ducal interference, creating a unique balance between feudal and mercantile governance.

advances.name: Kaperfahrt
advances.text: Pomeranian nobles and even some dukes have engaged in state-sanctioned piracy, seizing rival vessels to assert maritime control over the southern Baltic.

advances.name: Stralsund Defenses
advances.text: Stralsund's legendary walls, eleven gates, thirty watchtowers, proved impregnable even against Wallenstein's imperial army in 1628.

event.title: The Walls of Stralsund
event.text:
Albrecht von Wallenstein, the mightiest general in the Empire, has brought his army before the walls of Stralsund. The city council refused the Capitulation of Franzburg, and now the imperial host camps before eleven gates and thirty watchtowers. Wallenstein reportedly swore he would take the city even if it were chained to heaven itself.

But Stralsund endures. Danish and Swedish ships break the blockade to supply the garrison. The burghers man the walls alongside professional soldiers. After weeks of fruitless assault, the imperial army withdraws. Stralsund has proven that a well-fortified city, defended by determined citizens, can resist even the most powerful army in Europe.

options.text: The Griffin defies even heaven's chains

advances.name: Evangelical Reform
advances.text:
Pomerania embraced the Protestant Reformation early, transforming its churches and universities into centers of Lutheran scholarship.

Available in: Greifswalder Kollegium

advances.name: The Last Griffin
advances.text: Duke Bogislaw XIV, the last of the five-century Griffin dynasty, navigated the impossible politics of the Thirty Years' War with diplomatic skill.

advances.name: Wartime Resilience
advances.text: Though the Thirty Years' War destroyed two-thirds of Pomerania's population, the surviving communities rebuilt with grim determination.

advances.name: Urban Reconstruction
advances.text: After the devastation of the Thirty Years' War, Pomeranian towns slowly rebuilt their infrastructure and commercial networks.

advances.name: Junker Estates
advances.text: The Pomeranian landed nobility consolidated large agricultural estates, driving grain production for export through Baltic ports.

advances.name: Baltic Admiralty
advances.text: Under Swedish and later Prussian administration, Pomerania maintained its naval traditions, training sailors for the Baltic fleet.

advances.name: Academic Renaissance
advances.text: Greifswald University, now the oldest university in the Swedish realm, experiences a scholarly renaissance under enlightened patronage.

advances.name: Enlightenment Scholarship
advances.text: Greifswald's scholars contribute to the Enlightenment, producing works in natural philosophy, jurisprudence, and Baltic regional history.

advances.name: Stettin Industrialization
advances.text:
Stettin's Oder River port industrializes, with shipyards, foundries, and manufacturing transforming the medieval trading town into a modern city.

Available in: Amber Workshop

advances.name: Modern Shipyards
advances.text: Pomeranian shipyards adopt modern construction techniques, building faster and more capable vessels for the Baltic trade. The galeass, sailed by a handful of men, becomes the coast's own ship.

advances.name: Economic Integration
advances.text: Pomerania integrates into the broader German economic sphere, its ports connecting the agricultural hinterland to global markets.

destiny.name: The Griffin's Destiny
destiny.text: United Pomerania stands at a crossroads. The red griffin must choose its future: ducal authority forged in iron, or Hanseatic wealth built on amber and salt.

event.title: The Griffin's Destiny
event.text: Pomerania united: the red griffin now spreads its wings across the Baltic coast. But what manner of realm shall this be? The destiny of the Griffin House is not yet written. It falls to us to choose the path that will define Pomerania for centuries to come.

destiny.name: The Iron Crown
destiny.text: Secure Schwerin and assert Griffin authority over the neighboring duchies. The Pomeranian duke must prove he is more than a figurehead: he commands armies, not just counting houses.

event.title: The Iron Crown
event.text: Schwerin has fallen before Pomeranian arms. The Mecklenburg dukes, who once looked down upon the Griffins as mere coastal lordlings, now kneel before our banner. With a professional army at our command and the revenues of the Hanseatic ports funding our ambitions, the Griffin duke is no longer a first among equals: he is a sovereign in truth.

options.text: The Griffin commands, and the north obeys

destiny.name: The March South
destiny.text: Push into Brandenburg and seize Berlin and Rostock. The Oder is a Pomeranian river; its entire course should flow through Griffin lands.

event.title: The March South
event.text: Berlin and Rostock are ours. The Oder, from its headwaters to the sea, now flows through Griffin territory. Brandenburg's march lords have been humbled, and the Pomeranian duke gazes south across lands that once seemed impossibly distant. How shall we consolidate these conquests: through a standing army that answers only to the duke, or through border marches that project our power outward?

modifiers.name: Ducal Army
modifiers.text: The Griffin duke has established a professional standing army, replacing unreliable feudal levies with troops that answer only to the ducal crown.

modifiers.name: Border March
modifiers.text: Fortified border marches secure Pomerania's expanded frontiers, projecting Griffin power into neighboring lands.

destiny.name: Baltic Dominion
destiny.text: Forge a true Baltic kingdom stretching from Magdeburg to Konigsberg. The Griffin dynasty shall rule the greatest principality between the Elbe and the Vistula.

event.title: Baltic Dominion
event.text: From the Elbe to the Vistula, the red griffin flies over fortress and city alike. Magdeburg and Konigsberg (the seats of archbishops and grand masters) now answer to Pomerania. What began as a modest coastal duchy has become the dominant power of the North German Plain. The Griffin dynasty has achieved what seemed impossible. Shall we rule through military might, or through the institutions of governance?

options.text: Our armies are the foundation of our power

modifiers.name: Iron Scepter
modifiers.text: Pomerania's military machine is the terror of northern Europe, its veterans hardened by decades of conquest.

options.text: We shall build institutions to govern

modifiers.name: The Griffin Throne
modifiers.text: The Griffin dynasty rules through sophisticated governance, binding vassals and subjects through institutional loyalty rather than fear alone.

destiny.name: The Amber Road
destiny.text: Seize the Hanseatic capital of Lubeck and establish Pomeranian commercial supremacy. Baltic amber, the gold of the north, shall flow through our ports.

event.title: The Amber Road
event.text: Lubeck, the Queen of the Hanse, flies the Griffin banner. The greatest commercial city in northern Europe is now a Pomeranian possession. Amber, salt, grain, and herring flow through our ports in quantities that would have staggered our ancestors. The Wendish Hanse has found its champion: not a league of squabbling merchants, but a unified duchy with the power to enforce free trade at sword-point if necessary.

options.text: The amber road leads to Pomerania

destiny.name: The Counting Houses
destiny.text: Build Stettin, the Oder port where the duchy's counting houses keep their ledgers, from a town into a city, fill the treasury, and ensure salt (the lifeblood of the herring trade) flows through the capital market.

conditions.text: Stettin is ours and has grown into a city

children.text: Salt is produced in the market
Salt is traded in the market

event.title: The Counting Houses
event.text: Stettin has grown into a city, and the counting houses of Stettin and Stralsund have become proper banks, handling letters of credit and exchange across the Baltic. Salt from Luneburg and Kolberg flows through our capital market, preserving the herring that is the staple of northern commerce. Shall we consolidate this wealth through monopolistic control, or through chartered guilds that attract talent from across Europe?

options.text: Establish monopoly control of key trades

modifiers.name: Salt Monopoly
modifiers.text: Pomeranian control of the Baltic salt trade has given the duchy unrivaled commercial leverage, drawing peoples and goods to its markets.

modifiers.name: Guild Charter
modifiers.text: Chartered guilds attract skilled craftsmen from across Europe to Pomeranian cities, though the cost of maintaining a peacetime military rises.

destiny.name: Mare Balticum
destiny.text: Dominate Baltic trade from Lubeck to Visby. Take Visby and the Scanian herring coast at Malmo, where the Peace of Stralsund once gave the towns the castles of the Sound, and enforce the Wendish League's monopoly over the northern seas.

event.title: Mare Balticum
event.text: The Baltic Sea is a Pomeranian lake. From Lubeck to Visby, the great entrepots of northern trade answer to the Wendish League under Griffin patronage. Our merchants trade in every port from Bergen to Novgorod. Our fleet enforces the peace of commerce. The wealth of the north flows through Pomeranian hands. Shall we open our ports to the world, or shall the merchant princes rule as sovereign lords of commerce?

options.text: Declare Pomeranian ports free and open

modifiers.name: Free Port
modifiers.text: Pomeranian ports are declared open to all nations, attracting merchants, spies, and innovators from every corner of the known world.

modifiers.name: Merchant Prince
modifiers.text: The great merchant families of Stralsund and Stettin govern as princes of commerce, their wealth and influence holding the realm together.

units.name: Pomeranian Coastal Militia
units.text: Armed burghers and coastal peasants trained in the defense of their walled towns, these militia are the backbone of Pomeranian self-defense.

units.name: Pomeranian Kogge
units.text: The sturdy Hanseatic cog, workhorse of Baltic trade. These broad-beamed vessels carry vast cargoes through the choppy northern waters and can be armed for war.

units.name: Pomeranian Schnigge
units.text: A shallow, swift vessel under sail and oar. The Hanse towns send such ships out as scouts and guard ships. Under a ducal letter the same ship is a privateer.

units.name: Stralsund Frigate
units.text: A purpose-built coastal defense vessel from Stralsund's shipyards, designed to patrol the narrow straits and defend Pomeranian harbors.

units.name: Pomeranian Galeass
units.text: The two-masted coasting trader of the Baltic, built in the yards of the Pomeranian coast. It is sailed by a handful of men and is lightly built and lightly armed.

buildings.name: Kompaniehaus
buildings.text: The house of a merchant company in a Hanse town of Pomerania. The shipmasters and the merchants who sail to the herring markets keep a hall, a common chest and a rule of their own here, and settle their contracts among themselves.

buildings.name: Vitte
buildings.text: A herring station on the beach by the fishing grounds: a fenced compound of booths kept by a Hanse town. In the season the catch is gutted, salted and packed in barrels for the Lenten trade, and the boats of the shore land more of it.

where.text: The location's raw material is Fish

buildings.name: Greifswalder Kollegium
buildings.text: A collegiate building of the University of Greifswald, one of the oldest centers of learning in northern Europe.

buildings.name: Coastal Bastion
buildings.text: Fortified harbor defenses inspired by Stralsund's legendary walls, designed to protect Pomeranian ports from naval assault.

buildings.name: Amber Workshop
buildings.text: A craftsmen's workshop where Baltic amber is turned into beads, polished and later inlaid with ivory for sale across the Hanseatic trading network.

buildings.name: Oder Warehouse
buildings.text: A commercial warehouse along the Oder River docks, storing grain, salt, and other goods flowing through Stettin's bustling trade network.

buildings.name: Griffinburg
buildings.text: A mighty ducal fortress-palace crowned with the red griffin, embodying the military authority of the Griffin dynasty over its Baltic dominion.

buildings.name: Stapelhaus
buildings.text: A grand Hanseatic staple house where goods are stored, weighed, and taxed before re-export, the commercial heart of the Wendish League.

list.name: Pomeranian Landtag
list.text: The estates assembly of the Duchy of Pomerania, comprising the prelates of the Cammin chapter, the resident nobility of the eastern and western Vorpommern circles, and deputies from the Hanseatic towns of Stettin, Stralsund, Greifswald, Anklam, and Stargard. The Greifen dukes summoned the Landtag to ratify monetary taxation, war funding, and ecclesiastical policy; its veto over extraordinary levies bound every duke to consensus and made the rare unitary session at Treptow an der Rega on 13 December 1534, where the estates jointly accepted the Lutheran Reformation, the foundational political event of sixteenth-century Pomerania.

list.name: Hofgericht zu Wolgast
list.text: The ducal high court Philip I established in his Wolgast residence in the 1530s, in which the duke himself sat in judgement as a deliberate assertion of princely justice over the Patrimonialgerichte of the noble Rittergueter. The Hofgericht recorded land disputes, criminal pleas of ducal interest, and appeals from the Hanseatic town courts; its written rolls became the legal archive that the Greifen chancery still consulted under Bogislaw XIV a century later, and the institutional foundation that both Swedish Pomerania's Tribunal in Greifswald and the Brandenburg-Prussian Hofgericht inherited intact after 1648.

list.name: Wendish Hanse Quarter
list.text: The federation of Stralsund, Stettin, Greifswald, Anklam, Demmin, Kolberg, and Stargard within the Wendish third of the Hanseatic League, granted its own representation at the Hansetag in Luebeck from the late thirteenth century. Stralsund alone fielded some three hundred vessels under its flag in the fourteenth century, second only to Luebeck in the Baltic. The patrician town councils retained jus civitatis, mint privilege, and admiralty over their hinterlands, paying the duke for protection rather than submitting to him, a constitutional anomaly that periodically broke into open revolt against the Greifen, as in the Stralsund risings of 1391 and 1407.

list.name: Bugenhagen Kirchenordnung
list.text: The Lutheran church constitution drafted by Doctor Pomeranus, Johannes Bugenhagen of Wollin, at the request of Dukes Barnim XI and Philip I in 1534-1535 and finally implemented in 1563. It dissolved the Cammin chapter's old patrimony, transferred the bishopric's revenues into ducal hands as a secular Stift, and reorganised parish life under superintendents responsible for poor relief, school instruction, and the catechetical examination of every household. The Pomeranian Reformation was as much an act of state administration as of theology, binding the Lutheran clergy to the ducal court and equipping the duchy with the literate parish infrastructure that would make Greifswald and Stralsund seedbeds of Pietist learning a century later.

list.name: Rittergut Gutsherrschaft
list.text: The manorial regime of the Pomeranian knightly estates, in which the Junker landlord exercised Gutsherrschaft over an enserfed peasantry: regulating marriages, extracting compulsory Gesindezwangsdienst from younger sons, and farming the demesne directly with corvee labour to ship Baltic grain westward through the Hanseatic ports. The peasant and shepherd regulation of 1616 codified the severest form of the system, and a quarter of all knightly estates passed to Swedish nobles after 1648 without disturbing a single peasant burden. The Rittergueter supplied the cavalry levy and the officer corps; their lords expected, and received, near-complete jurisdictional autonomy from the duke.
